nodes.title: ENTER - Corridor
nodes.text:
You make your way carefully into the dungeon corridor. Damp glistens on the walls, and the air is thick with dust. Feeling your way forward, your eyes slowly begin to adjust to the darkness.

“What have I forgotten to pack?” you ask yourself.

Oh well. Too late now.

You continue for perhaps half a mile without a single junction. The corridor gradually widens, opening into cavernous spaces in places, and you begin to realise that you are slowly but surely descending deeper underground.

You stop to rest.

The darkness around you has become thick and oppressive. You pull out a small flint lantern and strike it. A tiny flame catches on the oil-soaked mantle, casting a weak pool of light around you. You must thank that halfling you met in the Wasted Wizard; if you ever see him again, he parted with this lantern for a hot meal.

It isn’t much, but it is enough to see the tips of your boots and a short distance ahead.

You continue and begin to feel tired; the air is becoming shallow and hard to breath, suddley the corridr open into a junction; some cooler air blows over you like a breath, as though the dungeon itself is breathing! You stop and try not to worry.

As you take you next step you hear a runmble, out of instinct you throw yourself on the ground just in time to feel the ground shake and pieces of rock cover you from behind... 

Lights out!

Turn to 100

nodes.title: Goblin - Kitchen - Listen first
nodes.text:
You listen at the door and can hear voices behind. Sound like some goblins eating and auduing over their food!

"Give me that bone! you had your share! says one, " get your own you greedy oaf" cries another.

You figure if you let them argue it out maybe the'll be one or two less to gight should you wish to enter.

Do you wait? Go to #
Or burst in? Go to 13
Or return to the Junction? Go to 17

nodes.title: Stairs
nodes.text: Cold air rises from the darkness below.

nodes.title: Store Room
nodes.text: Only accessible if you have the Iron Key.

nodes.title: Troll Bridge
nodes.text: Before you spans an ancient and very unsafe-looking bridge; you cannot really see what is on the other side, but you think you can see a slight glow, maybe a torch? Halfway across the bridge is a lever.

nodes.title: Troll Den
nodes.text: You peer into the dark cave, which slowley becomes wide and forks off into 2 forections. Bones littler the floors and there is the smell of something boiling down the right tunnel.

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.text:
The Ghost Bell

Throughout time, or as long as most can remember, the bells of Dragonreach have always been a guiding light to the people of this land, not just to meet on religious days and holidays but also as an early warning of invasion and danger. Some 300 bells are situated in Dragonreach, and the people value them all. A selection of carefully chosen bell wardens would monitor these powerful and ancient bells. Tarak the healer is one of the chosen wardens; he is proud and honoured to have been chosen.

He would go about his usual duties as a respected medical and spiritual guide to look after not just the people in is ward but in his spare time he would keep and take great care in the bell duties, restoring, repairing and keeping the bells mechanically sound.

One spring morning Tarak is preparing his bags and sachels with herbs and potions to make his visits, he cares a great deal about his local people and they rely on him for health and spiritual guidance. He always takes stock, sometimes very early in the morning, scanning the heavily laden shelves he has built up over the years and is proud of his collection. Some items in Tarak's collection may seem useless to the untrained eye and there's a a reson for that, a healer would never make up a potion, label it and put it on the shelf for later use. With all the talk and gossip around the Dargonmarch taverns, what if the Shadow Army did invade and they got their hands on his potions? That could be catastrophic. No, an experienced healer would make up the potions as they need them, and his recipes would- well, they would die with him. 

Tarak has, this morning, run out of one vital herb, the herb Travelling Star, a herb needed to cure poison, that and a few other elements, but he needs some and urgently. There is talk of some locals becoming very ill recently due to unsavoury characters poisoning the well. He fears these may be spies for the oncoming attack.

nodes.title: Troll rubbish shoot
nodes.text: You rummage through the piles of stinking bones and discarded previous adventures, only to find a chain mechanism. Will you pull the chain or back away?

nodes.title: Goblin - Kitchen Open without checking
nodes.text:
You burst into what looks like a small kitchen or eating area to find 3 large goblins staring back at you.

Roll your dexterity or above to quickly slam the door and block it with a nearby latch. This is a heavy, strong door and as long as you hold that latch down, they won't get out.

nodes.title: Goblin - Kitchen
nodes.text:
Now all the goblins lay slain you look around. This is dirty place that would never get any reviews on Doogle (the wasted wizard notice board). There grease covered burnt pots stacked high, bones and old meat strewn across the floor and the large round table in the middle of the room seems to have a sricky sunstance.

nodes.title: Junction
nodes.text:
It's a while before you come round but when you you notice the way back is now blocked by a rock fall. You feel this is now a one way trip and take stock, no harm done as such but you sit for a while and rest. You eventually get to your feet, you take a short drink from you water flask and hope you can find more later and you walk a little futher to a junction.

To the right are some steps, hewn out of the rock, but clearly an ascending route to a higher ledge.
